Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)
The supplied file contains diagnosis code only; the model architecture and sequence representation computation are not shown. Diagnosis uses `item_emb.weight`, `log2feats(sequence)` for per-position sequence features, and `predict_score(features, items)` for candidate logits. It evaluates all valid training positions rather than explicitly selecting a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks
`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied compatibility object and accesses its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Reviews and histories are stored but unused by these probes. The adapter must expose the trained model through the required view contract.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape B × L. The margin probe switches the model to evaluation mode, disables gradients, converts sequences to NumPy, computes features, and scores paired positive/negative items. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics
- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings with seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the mean to [0,1]. High values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 represents zero average cosine similarity, not necessarily unhealthy embeddings.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Over at most ten loader batches, computes positive minus negative logits. Reports the mean, empirical tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and smaller error fractions generally indicate stronger sampled training separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts positive and negative item categories in weak-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top twenty. Counts are unnormalized. Categories are unavailable in this task, so these lists should remain empty rather than use invented metadata.

# Perturbation & Tests
There are no sequence perturbations, shuffling tests, or sensitivity checks. Random embedding sampling reduces computation; supplied negatives provide the ranking comparison.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations
`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing five scalar metrics plus the nested category breakdown. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting grounded JSON interpretation.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation diversity, temporal sensitivity, simulator traits, or gradients. Results depend on sampled negatives and logit scale. Empty margin samples return zeros, potentially masking missing evidence; evaluation mode is not restored afterward.

Recent research separates topical similarity from intent satisfaction. [FollowIR (2024/2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.23841) evaluates instruction-sensitive retrieval; [Hard-BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) addresses false negatives introduced by hard sampling. Implication: broadly related items make useful diagnostic distractors, but unobserved items should not automatically become confirmed negatives. A practical adaptation is BM25 or TF-IDF over public titles/descriptions, comparing specific recent-interest matches against candidates sharing only broad vocabulary. Report pairwise score margins and ranking accuracy where validation relevance is observed; lexical overlap alone cannot establish relevance.

Complementarity, substitution and compatibility require separate evidence. The [2024 complementary-recommendation survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16135) describes asymmetric relations and coexistence of substitutes and complements; [Allegro’s 2026 work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063) explicitly distinguishes co-purchase from products that work together. For this task, an evidence-grounded adaptation would extract explicit model identifiers, connectors, dimensions, formats, artists and series from available text. Record supported matches, explicit conflicts and unknown specifications separately, retaining supporting text spans. Measure attribute coverage and conflict rates with clear denominators; abstain from compatibility claims when evidence is missing. Near-duplicate titles indicate possible redundancy, not ownership satisfaction or lack of replacement intent.

[User-feedback research (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09869) distinguishes intentional feedback from ordinary consumption behavior. Accordingly, histories provide interest signals, not observed satisfaction, diversity preferences or purchase intent. Treat feedback-inspired diagnostics as hypotheses, validate ranking changes using the common macro HR@10, and keep evidence-coverage diagnostics distinct from recommendation-quality metrics. These adaptations require no downloaded pretrained weights.

KDD 2025’s [Lost in Sequence](https://doi.org/10.1145/3711896.3737035) compares original versus shuffled histories during training and inference, plus representation similarity: SASRec deteriorates substantially under shuffling, whereas several LLM recommenders change little. [Demystifying Sequential Recommendations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) (2025) searches for minimal history edits that change recommendations, providing a complementary counterfactual explanation approach. These results motivate probing sensitivity, but sensitivity alone does not establish useful temporal reasoning.

Practical adaptation: reserve next-event targets within training histories; compare each intact prefix against recent-event deletion, equally sized older-event deletion, full shuffling, and shuffling that preserves the final item. Replace selected events with different items matched by training interaction-frequency bins to separate item identity from popularity effects. The 2024 [PAUDRec paper](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0957417423019310) motivates distinguishing popularity effects from evolving interests, although these proposed matched controls are an experimental adaptation rather than its reported protocol. Calibrate probes using synthetic processes with known dependencies: last-item transitions, order-invariant historical preferences, repeated-interest signals, and popularity-only targets. Treat perturbations as model-behavior evidence, acknowledge that edited histories may be unrealistic, and select improvements using the unchanged macro validation HR@10. ## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)
The supplied file contains diagnosis code only; the model architecture and sequence representation computation are not shown. Diagnosis uses `item_emb.weight`, `log2feats(sequence)` for per-position sequence features, and `predict_score(features, items)` for candidate logits. It evaluates all valid training positions rather than explicitly selecting a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks
`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the supplied compatibility object and accesses its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Reviews and histories are stored but unused by these probes. The adapter must expose the trained model through the required view contract.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape B × L. The margin probe switches the model to evaluation mode, disables gradients, converts sequences to NumPy, computes features, and scores paired positive/negative items. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics
- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings with seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the mean to [0,1]. High values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 represents zero average cosine similarity, not necessarily unhealthy embeddings.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Over at most ten loader batches, computes positive minus negative logits. Reports the mean, empirical tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and smaller error fractions generally indicate stronger sampled training separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts positive and negative item categories in weak-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top twenty. Counts are unnormalized. Categories are unavailable in this task, so these lists should remain empty rather than use invented metadata.

# Perturbation & Tests
There are no sequence perturbations, shuffling tests, or sensitivity checks. Random embedding sampling reduces computation; supplied negatives provide the ranking comparison.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations
`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing five scalar metrics plus the nested category breakdown. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting grounded JSON interpretation.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation diversity, temporal sensitivity, simulator traits, or gradients. Results depend on sampled negatives and logit scale. Empty margin samples return zeros, potentially masking missing evidence; evaluation mode is not restored afterward.
